title: NOONAN SYNDROME-LIKE DISORDER WITH LOOSE ANAGEN HAIR 1

relationships.phenotype: NOONAN SYNDROME-LIKE DISORDER WITH LOOSE ANAGEN HAIR 1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 (NSLH1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SHOC2 gene (602775) on chromosome 10q25.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 (NSLH1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SHOC2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Twenty-five subjects with a relatively consistent phenotype previously termed Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair (MIM607721) shared the 4A>G missense change in SHOC2 (producing an S2G amino acid substitution)
checks.explanation: The paper shows SHOC2 mutation causes the disorder but never says the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 gene is located on chromosome 10q25.
checks.evidence_quote: Resequencing of coding exons for the best candidate, SHOC2, in a NS cohort including 96 individuals
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature. The paper itself does not give 10q25.

paragraphs.text: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is a RASopathy that shares features with Noonan syndrome, including characteristic facial features, short stature, and congenital heart defects (particularly dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects). Distinguishing features are hair abnormalities: hair that is easily pluckable, sparse, thin, and slow-growing (loose anagen hair). Other features include growth hormone deficiency, darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis, hypernasal voice, and cognitive deficits, often with hyperactive behavior.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is a RASopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients 1–3 were originally clinically diagnosed with Costello syndrome or a related rasopathy
checks.explanation: The paper frames Noonan syndrome and SHOC2-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair as rasopathies.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares with Noonan syndrome characteristic facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: While their facial features seemed typical for NS (Fig. 1a)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares with Noonan syndrome short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: We present three children with short stature, the same facial phenotype, macrocephaly
checks.explanation: Short stature is reported in all three children, whose condition the authors describe as Noonan-like.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares with Noonan syndrome congenital heart defects, particularly mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects.
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiac anomalies were observed in the majority of the cases, with dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects significantly overrepresented compared with the general NS population.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is distinguished by hair abnormalities: hair that is easily pluckable, sparse, thin, and slow-growing (loose anagen hair).
checks.evidence_quote: hair anomalies including easily pluckable, sparse, thin, slow growing hair. In twelve subjects, a diagnosis of loose anagen hair was confirmed by microscopic examination of pulled hairs.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Features of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 include growth hormone deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: short neck with redundant skin, severe GH deficiency
checks.explanation: The abstract reports severe GH deficiency.

checks.claim: Features of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 include darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of them also exhibited darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Features of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 include hypernasal voice.
checks.evidence_quote: The voice was characteristically hypernasal.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Features of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 include cognitive deficits, often with hyperactive behavior.
checks.evidence_quote: mild psychomotor delay with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports mild psychomotor delay with ADHD, which matches cognitive deficits with hyperactive behavior.

paragraphs.text: Mazzanti et al. (2003) described patients with a Noonan-like phenotype associated with loose anagen hair, which they proposed as a distinct entity. In addition to Noonan-like facial features and short stature, the patients had easily pluckable, sparse, slow-growing hair, and growth hormone deficiency was noted.

checks.claim: Mazzanti et al. (2003) described patients with a Noonan-like phenotype associated with loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: We postulate that these children may represent a distinct, previously unreported syndrome that we would name "Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair".
checks.explanation: The authors describe a Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.

checks.claim: Mazzanti et al. (2003) proposed Noonan-like phenotype with loose anagen hair as a distinct entity.
checks.evidence_quote: We postulate that these children may represent a distinct, previously unreported syndrome
checks.explanation: The authors propose the condition as a distinct entity.

checks.claim: The patients described by Mazzanti et al. (2003) had Noonan-like facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: Their appearance, not completely typical of Noonan syndrome
checks.explanation: The children shared a facial phenotype and the condition is called Noonan-like, but the abstract says their appearance was not completely typical of Noonan syndrome.

checks.claim: The patients described by Mazzanti et al. (2003) had short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: We present three children with short stature
checks.explanation: The abstract reports short stature.

checks.claim: The patients described by Mazzanti et al. (2003) had easily pluckable, sparse, slow-growing hair.
checks.evidence_quote: the unusual aspect of the hair, defined as loose anagen hair syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions loose anagen hair but not the specific traits (easily pluckable, sparse, slow-growing). These may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Growth hormone deficiency was noted in the patients described by Mazzanti et al. (2003).
checks.evidence_quote: severe GH deficiency
checks.explanation: The abstract reports severe GH deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Cordeddu et al. (2009) delineated the clinical phenotype of patients carrying the same SHOC2 mutation, noting a distinctive combination of Noonan-like features with loose anagen hair, short stature frequently associated with growth hormone deficiency, darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis, hypernasal voice, cardiac defects with frequent mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects, and cognitive deficits with hyperactive behavior.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) delineated the clinical phenotype of patients carrying the same SHOC2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Review of the clinical features of the SHOC2 mutation-positive individuals revealed a consistent phenotype, previously termed Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had a distinctive combination of Noonan-like features with loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: these subjects appeared to share a phenotype that was characterized by an unusual combination of features observed in disorders of the neuro-cardio-facial-cutaneous disorders family
checks.explanation: Combined with the NS-like face and confirmed loose anagen hair, this supports the claim.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had short stature frequently associated with growth hormone deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: they exhibited reduced growth, which was frequently associated with proven GH deficiency
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of them also exhibited darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had hypernasal voice.
checks.evidence_quote: The voice was characteristically hypernasal.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had cardiac defects with frequent mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects.
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiac anomalies were observed in the majority of the cases, with dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects significantly overrepresented compared with the general NS population.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had cognitive deficits with hyperactive behavior.
checks.evidence_quote: cognitive deficits, distinctive hyperactive behaviour that improved with age in most subjects
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous SHOC2 mutation identified by Cordeddu et al. (2009) occurred de novo in the patients tested, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The heterozygous SHOC2 mutation identified by Cordeddu et al. (2009) occurred de novo in the patients tested.
checks.evidence_quote: We observed 21 with the 4A>G missense change and proved that mutations were de novo in twelve families from which parental DNAs were available.
checks.explanation: The paper confirms de novo occurrence in the families tested but never states that the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The de novo occurrence of the heterozygous SHOC2 mutation is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1.
checks.evidence_quote: providing evidence that the change was a de novo mutation associated with the disease. For these subjects, DNAs from several tissues were available and all harboured the S2G mutation, providing evidence that the defect was inherited through the germline.
checks.explanation: The paper reports de novo germline mutations but never states autosomal dominant inheritance; that is an inference.

paragraphs.text: A similar phenotype, Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-2 (NSLH2), is caused by mutation in the PPP1CB gene.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-2 (NSLH2), a phenotype similar to NSLH1, is caused by mutation in the PPP1CB gene.
checks.evidence_quote: this novel RASopathy-PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair-shares great similarity to Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair that closely resembles NSLH. It calls PPP1CB 'a novel gene associated with RASopathies' and reports the recurrent p.Pro49Arg mutation.

paragraphs.text: Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a recurrent heterozygous c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution, in patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair. The mutation arose de novo. Functional studies showed that the substitution introduced an N-myristoylation site, resulting in aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2 and its constitutive targeting to the plasma membrane, which impaired its translocation to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation and enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific manner.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a recurrent heterozygous c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution, in patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed an A-to-G transition at position 4 of the gene, predicting the Ser2Gly amino acid substitution (S2G), in four unrelated individuals
checks.explanation: The recurrent c.4A>G (S2G) change is supported, but the paper never states that it is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutation identified by Cordeddu et al. (2009) arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: proved that mutations were de novo in twelve families from which parental DNAs were available
checks.explanation: De novo status was confirmed where parental DNA was available.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that the SHOC2 S2G substitution introduced an N-myristoylation site, resulting in aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2.
checks.evidence_quote: SHOC2S2G incorporated [3H]-myristic acid, while the wild type protein and the disease-unrelated SHOC2S2A did not.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that SHOC2 S2G is constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: This acquired fatty acid modification, a unique finding for inherited human disease, results in constitutive membrane targeting
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that SHOC2 S2G has impaired translocation to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation.
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in aberrant targeting of SHOC2 to the plasma membrane and impaired translocation to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that SHOC2 S2G enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific manner.
checks.evidence_quote: Expression of SHOC2(S2G) in vitro enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific fashion.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) identified the SHOC2 S2G mutation in Japanese patients with a phenotype in the Noonan syndrome spectrum including loose anagen hair.

checks.claim: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) identified the SHOC2 S2G mutation in Japanese patients with a phenotype in the Noonan syndrome spectrum including loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: We found the previously identified p.S2G mutation in eight of our patients.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports finding the S2G mutation in patients in the Noonan spectrum who had easily pluckable/loose anagen hair. It does not state that the patients were Japanese, which may be in the full text.

allelic_variants.name: SHOC2, SER2GLY

paragraphs.text: In patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair, Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a de novo heterozygous c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution. The mutation created an N-myristoylation site, causing aberrant myristoylation and constitutive plasma membrane targeting of SHOC2, and enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific fashion.

checks.evidence_quote: revealed an A-to-G transition at position 4 of the gene, predicting the Ser2Gly amino acid substitution (S2G), in four unrelated individuals
checks.explanation: The de novo c.4A>G (S2G) change is supported, but heterozygosity is not stated in the paper.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutation created an N-myristoylation site, causing aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2.
checks.evidence_quote: shared the 4A>G missense change in SHOC2 (producing an S2G amino acid substitution) that introduces an N-myristoylation site
checks.explanation: Stated directly, and myristoylation was confirmed experimentally.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutation caused constitutive plasma membrane targeting of SHOC2.

checks.explanation: Stated directly.
